title: The rationality problem for multinorm one tori: the quasi-permutation theorem for $G_{m,\nu}=C_{m}\times D_{2^{\nu}}$ (Theorem 6.7)
author: Sumito Hasegawa, Kazuki Kanai, Yasuhiro Oki
work: The rationality problem for multinorm one tori
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the theorem printed as Theorem 6.7 of "The rationality problem for multinorm one tori" (source0.tex lines 1942--1949, source label thm:nlqp), delivered together with the article's own complete proof of it at source0.tex lines 1951--2132 (182 lines, one adjacent proof environment). The theorem is the article's key result for the 2-power case: for every odd positive integer m and every positive integer nu it proves that the G_{m,nu}-lattice J_{G_{m,nu}/H_{m,nu}} attached to G_{m,nu}=C_m x D_{2^nu} and to the two cyclic subgroups H_{m,nu}={<tau_{2^nu}>, <sigma_{2^nu} tau_{2^nu}>} is quasi-permutation, that is, it fits into an exact sequence 0 -> J -> R -> F -> 0 with R and F permutation. The proof is complete inside the retained span. It is not a routine exercise: the author constructs an explicit homomorphism Phi_{m,nu} from a direct sum R_{m,nu} of permutation lattices onto I_{m,nu}, exhibiting the cokernel (Z/mZ)^{2^{nu-1}-1} by four displayed identities and proving surjectivity of Phi_{m,nu} by induction on nu; obtains the exact sequence 0 -> U_{m,nu} -> R_{m,nu} -> I_{m,nu} -> 0; proves a two-part Claim on U_{m,nu} cap R_{m,nu,*} whose first part rests on a rank computation (2^{nu+1}(m+1)+1)-(2^{nu+1}m-1) compared through a snake-lemma argument and the article's coflabby-resolution lemma; and then runs a second induction on nu through two explicitly built homomorphisms Xi_{m,nu,1} and Xi_{m,nu,2} to establish the isomorphism (eq:fmns) U_{m,nu} + S_{m,nu} = (U_{m,nu} cap R_{m,nu,*}^{-}) + S'_{m,nu} + S_{m,nu} which exhibits the required quasi-permutation. The argument invokes four auxiliary results of the same article - its Theorem 6.1 and its Lemmas 6.3, 6.4, 6.5 and 6.6, all delivered in statement form - plus the flabby and coflabby resolution machinery of Endo-Miyata, Voskresenskii and Colliot-Thelene-Sansuc; no step is delegated outside the retained spans and no gap is left to the reader. It is rated H3 rather than H2 because a solver must control flabby and coflabby resolutions of G-lattices over Z[G], the fixed and cofixed parts of a lattice under a normal subgroup, a four-hypothesis isomorphism lemma, and two nested inductions on nu at once, and must reproduce an explicit lattice presentation for the whole family of groups C_m x D_{2^nu}; that chain of reasoning is research level and well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
